comparison.objective: Select and mount the undamaged grinding wheel with the complete ordered flange/blotter stack, tighten it safely, and verify secure mounting; candidate instead adjusts and locks an already-assembled gripper opening stop at a target angle.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-871 emphasizes inspection choice, repeated coaxial insertion of keyed and annular parts, spindle restraint, and torque-window tightening. The candidate emphasizes simultaneous driver-and-wrench counterholding so a screw setting does not rotate while its jam nut is locked, followed by tool withdrawal and articulation.
comparison.success_condition: PR-871 scores ordered stack completion, nut seating below an irreversible overtorque limit, released spindle-lock/hand clearance, low slip in a braked spin, and limited axial motion under tug. The candidate scores target-angle accuracy, nut retention, three close-open returns, at most 2° drift, and sustained 30 mm clearance, with revocation on locking or retention failure.
comparison.reason: Both include nut tightening, clearance, and post-tightening functional checks, but PR-871 tests safe ordered wheel-stack assembly and clamp adequacy, whereas the candidate's defining ability is preserving an adjustable screw setting against coupled locknut reaction.
